proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(T\geq 1\), a member of \(\mathfrak M_{d,k,T}(\epsilon,B)\), and hence its common nominal objects \(P,\rho,b,\pi,o,r,g,h\).  Assume the displayed premise of the theorem:
\[
 \mathbb E_{\Pr_{P,\rho,b,o}}
 \sup_{q\in\Theta(P)}|M_T(q)|
 \leq \frac{511B d^{dk}}{\epsilon}\sqrt T.
\tag{1}
\]
By \(\texttt{lem:poisson-martingale}\), after adding a constant to \(h\) if necessary, we may and do take \(0\leq h(z)\leq B\) for every \(z\in\mathcal S\), and, for every \(q\in\Theta(P)\),
\[
 T\{Q^{\mathrm{full}}_{q,T}(X_{0:T})-g\}
 =\alpha_0(q)K_{\pi}h-\alpha_T(q)K_{\pi}h+M_T(q)
\tag{2}
\]
holds \(\Pr_{P,\rho,b,o}\)-almost surely.  This identity may be used simultaneously over \(q\): the full-path space \(\mathcal S^{T+1}\) is finite and its law is common to all \(q\in\Theta(P)\) by \(\texttt{def:factual-record-law}\); hence an almost-sure identity valid for a fixed \(q\) holds at every path having positive common probability, and therefore at every such path for every \(q\).  The kernel \(K_{\pi}\) is stochastic by its definition from the controlled transition law \(P\), and each \(\alpha_t(q)\) is a probability distribution by the definition of the conditional filter.  Therefore
\[
 0\leq \alpha_t(q)K_{\pi}h\leq B
 \qquad(t\in\{0,T\}),
\tag{3}
\]
so the difference of the two boundary terms in (2) has absolute value at most \(B\).  Dividing (2) by the positive integer \(T\) and using (3) gives
\[
 \left|Q^{\mathrm{full}}_{q,T}(X_{0:T})-g\right|
 \leq \frac{B+|M_T(q)|}{T}.
\tag{4}
\]

The scalar \(g\) is common to all \(q\in\Theta(P)\), because the nominal kernel \(K_{\pi}\), reward \(r\), and the Poisson equation are fixed while the compatible response law varies.  Hence the definition of the full-record diameter and (4) imply, almost surely,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 D^{\mathrm{full}}_T(P,\rho,b,X_{0:T})
 &=\sup_{q\in\Theta(P)}Q^{\mathrm{full}}_{q,T}(X_{0:T})
   -\inf_{q\in\Theta(P)}Q^{\mathrm{full}}_{q,T}(X_{0:T})\\
 &\leq 2\sup_{q\in\Theta(P)}
       \left|Q^{\mathrm{full}}_{q,T}(X_{0:T})-g\right|\\
 &\leq \frac{2B}{T}
       +\frac{2}{T}\sup_{q\in\Theta(P)}|M_T(q)|.
\end{aligned}
\tag{5}
\]
Taking expectations in (5) and applying (1), with \(m=d^{dk}=|\mathcal R|\), yields
\[
 \mathbb E_{\Pr_{P,\rho,b,o}}D^{\mathrm{full}}_T(P,\rho,b,X_{0:T})
 \leq \frac{2B}{T}+\frac{1022Bm}{\epsilon\sqrt T}.
\tag{6}
\]
Here \(m\geq1\), \(0<\epsilon\leq1\), and \(T\geq1\).  Consequently
\[
 \frac{2B}{T}
 \leq \frac{2Bm}{\epsilon\sqrt T},
\tag{7}
\]
including when \(B=0\), and (6)--(7) give
\[
 \mathbb E_{\Pr_{P,\rho,b,o}}D^{\mathrm{full}}_T(P,\rho,b,X_{0:T})
 \leq \frac{1024B d^{dk}}{\epsilon\sqrt T}
 =\frac{C_{d,k,\epsilon,B}}{\sqrt T}.
\tag{8}
\]

By \(\texttt{lem:coarsening-domination}\), the common factual-record law from \(\texttt{def:factual-record-law}\) satisfies
\[
 \mathbb E_{\Pr_{P,\rho,b,o}}
 D_T(P,\rho,b,o,E_T)
 \leq
 \mathbb E_{\Pr_{P,\rho,b,o}}
 D^{\mathrm{full}}_T(P,\rho,b,X_{0:T}),
\tag{9}
\]
and combining (8) with (9) proves the stated root-\(T\) bound.  Finally, the declared reward range \(0\leq r\leq1\) implies that every conditional average \(Q_{q,T}(P,\rho,b,o,e)\) lies in \([0,1]\) whenever \(\Pr_{P,\rho,b,o}(E_T=e)>0\).  Thus \(D_T(P,\rho,b,o,e)\leq1\), and taking the smaller of this logical bound and (8)--(9) proves
\[
 \mathbb E_{\Pr_{P,\rho,b,o}}D_T(P,\rho,b,o,E_T)
 \leq
 \min\left\{1,\frac{C_{d,k,\epsilon,B}}{\sqrt T}\right\}.
\]
No step divides by a response mass \(q_f\), and no step assumes contraction of any conditional counterfactual kernel \(L_q\); the only uniform process input is exactly the conditional premise (1).
